name: Fund Strategy Sandbox and Edge

positioning.oneLineSummary: Defines the fund's investable sandbox and requires observable evidence for the team's claimed founder-access, selection, and support edge.
positioning.productLabel: Fund Strategy Sandbox — based on Mahendra Ramsinghani's public third-edition chapter summaries
notAClaimOf: a broad mandate being an edge

attribution.display: Based on Mahendra Ramsinghani's public third-edition chapter summaries

neutralParaphrase: Express strategy as the intersection of team expertise, market opportunity, stage, sector, geography, target founder, check, and support model. Permit documented exceptions inside a bounded sandbox. Test any claimed edge through evidence of differentiated sourcing, judgment, founder choice, or post-investment help.

locator.value: Public chapter summary: strategy, sandbox flexibility, white spaces, competition among funds, and edge dimensions
Public chapter summary: manager expertise, strategy, team stability, and consistency

requiredConditions: A user-confirmed Fund Policy or explicitly labeled default profile exists.
Strategy dimensions and permissible exceptions are machine-readable.
Claimed edge has observable evidence and a relevant time window.
The company thesis remains separate from fund fit.

requiredEvidence.description: Stage, sector, geography, business model, check, ownership, risk, support, and exclusion policy.
Experience, access, sourcing, selection, founder preference, and support evidence relevant to the target market.
Current investable company volume and competitive fund landscape within the sandbox.

decisionQuestions: What exact opportunity set is the fund designed to access?
Why is this team unusually suited to source, select, or help within it?
Does the current deal fit the sandbox?
If it is an exception, what is the reason and portfolio cost?
What evidence would falsify the claimed edge?
positiveSignals: Strategy dimensions are explicit and mutually compatible.
Opportunity set is large enough for planned deployment.
Edge appears in actual source attribution or founder choice.
Exceptions are rare, documented, and budgeted.
Team capacity matches the stated support model.
redFlags: The strategy is simply 'best companies anywhere.'
Edge consists only of generic network or brand language.
Policy changes whenever a fashionable deal appears.
The fund lacks enough relevant deal flow for construction targets.
A market default is displayed as the user's real policy.
disconfirmingEvidence: Most strong deals arrive outside the claimed channel.
Founders choose competing funds for the same promised edge.
Team experience is dated or not relevant to current stage.
Exceptions consume disproportionate capital or attention.
The investable opportunity set cannot support planned company count.
contraindications: Do not treat strategy fit as company quality.
Do not infer edge from prestige alone.
Do not use this card as an investment veto until policy is user-confirmed.

instructions: Map the deal against every strategy dimension.
Evaluate claimed edge using observable evidence.
Classify in-sandbox, documented exception, or out-of-scope.
Send exception costs to portfolio construction and deterministic policy.

sourceReliability.low: Strategy comes only from public marketing.
sourceReliability.medium: Internal policy exists but implementation evidence is partial.
sourceReliability.high: User-confirmed policy, historical decisions, and attribution data agree.

evidenceStrength.low: Edge is asserted without observed outcomes.
evidenceStrength.medium: Relevant experience and some sourcing or founder evidence exist.
evidenceStrength.high: Repeated sourcing, selection, or support evidence distinguishes the team.

evidenceCoverage.low: Only sector and stage are known.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Policy is mostly covered but edge or opportunity-set evidence is partial.
evidenceCoverage.high: Policy, edge, opportunity set, competition, capacity, and exceptions are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.medium: A default policy is explicitly labeled and user-editable.
applicabilityConfidence.high: A current user-confirmed policy is pinned.

judgmentConfidence.low: Only tentative fit questions are supportable.
judgmentConfidence.medium: Strategy fit is clear but edge remains uncertain.
judgmentConfidence.high: Fit, edge, opportunity set, and exception impact are well supported.

promotionRequirements: Validate Fund Policy schema with GPs and LPs.
empiricalQualifications: Emerging strategies may lack historical proof.
Public fund positioning may differ from actual policy.

rights.notes: Public chapter doctrine is paraphrased; policy schema and exception gates are product synthesis.

openIssues: Define default policy profiles by stage.
